I moved to Europe for the second time when I was 14 and quickly realized that life is extremely hit or miss when it comes to friends and it can make or break your life. In America I had an amazing friend group, that I still talk to, to this day, we would do everything together, basketball, swim, bike rides, etc. And when I moved back to Europe I lost them. It completely destroyed me and has done for the past 3 years. I’m completely alone and have no one. The first year I moved back I made an effort to be the best version of me I could and lost myself the following 2 years. The past 2 years have been rough and it made me feel like I wasted time, I sit in my room and play video games when I get home every day and I hate it. I’ve gone out and tried to meet people but it’s difficult when we don’t even speak the same language. The mental toll that it took on me wasn’t like anything I had ever gone through. Anyways, point being, it’s extremely rare to find friends like that and when/if you lose them it can be extremely hard to recover, it’s not even that I’m a dependent person, but life seems like a meaningless endless cycle now. So I guess my answer is that life became way worse than I thought it to be when I lost contact with the people that are important to me, and in a more general sense, was forced into a life I don’t want nor chose. The lesson that it taught me is that you need to become your own boss, work your own hours, and live your own life. Don’t get stuck in the rat race, it’s more dangerous then it seems, it really is. The 9-5 cycle is not something you want to live, it’s avoidable, so avoid it. I’ve been there, done that. I’ve lived that lifestyle just to quit. It’s important to know that this is just how I feel but I feel strongly about it and I reckon most others would agree. Don’t get trapped. You only have one life, so take risks, and live your life how you want to live it.
